cases.title: A downpipe places in a few seconds: every source landing read is under 1.5 s and DP completes under 10 s (BUG-1228)
cases.plan_item: BUG-1228 (B-004, train C-76 PR 1837); DP, OF and CDFW speed
cases.expected: With the timing log ON, DP at 150000,-80000 prints 'Downpipe placed. Tag: DP<n>.' and offers the next DP; Esc stops it; one new DOWNPIPE DYNAMIC WITH MASK insert exists; no 'could not be refreshed'. The CE log gains at least one '[BUG-1228] Source landing index read in N ms' line and one '[BUG-1228] Source change read in N ms' line, every one with N under 1,500 and 'reads each object once: on', none 'off'; and 'Command outcome: DP completed N ms' with N under 10,000. On Civil 3.0.85 the same DP took 27,600 to 32,400 ms (four reads of about 5 s each).
cases.why_not_unit: The time is spent reading the real drawing's 1,083 objects and 49 pipes; the unit tests prove the same answers on made-up objects, never the time on a real drawing.
not_automated: OF, CDFW and a DP dropped on a pipe end use the same reads but are not timed here (the report's later twins N31b and N31c, to be renumbered).

The 10,000 ms budget includes the runner's own wait at the next DP prompt; a slow PC or a busy disk can add seconds. A FAIL on that check alone with every read line under 1,500 ms is worth one re-run in a new start before it is called a fault.

If the timing switch is not picked up from the SETTING line, no [BUG-1228] line is written and the 'has' checks fail: that is a setup fault, not a product fault (the record of the CE log tells which).
